items.title: The economics of attention in the age of AI
items.summary_original: When machines pay attention, what deserves ours? AI filtering the information reaching us, shaping the economics of human attention. AI-generated visual, Aurélie Radom © For decades, digital products competed for our attention. The web put information everywhere, social networks turned it into a constant stream, and smartphones made it always accessible, making attention the scarce resource. Entire industries were built around capturing it: feeds, notifications, recommendations, autoplay. The basic logic was simple. If information is everywhere but attention is scarce, the product that wins is the product that gets our attention. We became very good at this. items.title: david altrath reveals the timber world inside germany’s motorway chapel
items.summary_original: david altrath photographs germany's autobahnkirche David Altrath turns his camera toward the Autobahnkirche Siegerland, a roadside chapel by schneider+schumacher beside the A45 motorway near Wilnsdorf, Germany . His photographic series focuses on the sculptural geometry of the building, tracing the transition from its stark white exterior to the warm, intricate timber structure inside. Completed in 2013, the chapel was designed as a place for travelers to pause beside the motorway. Its exterior translates the familiar pictogram of a church into a three-dimensional architectural form, with two pointed spires rising above a folded white volume. Altrath photographs this silhouette from close and distant perspectives, isolating its sharp edges, sloping planes and openings against the surroundi
items.title_de: David Altrath enthüllt die Welt des Holzes in Deutschlands Autobahnkapelle
items.summary_de: David Altrath fotografiert die deutsche Autobahnkirche David Altrath richtet seine Kamera auf die Autobahnkirche Siegerland, eine Straßenkapelle von schneider+schumacher neben der Autobahn A45 in der Nähe von Wilnsdorf, Deutschland. Seine Fotoserie konzentriert sich auf die skulpturale Geometrie des Gebäudes und zeichnet den Übergang von seinem strahlend weißen Äußeren zur warmen, komplexen Holzstruktur im Inneren nach. Die 2013 fertiggestellte Kapelle war als Raststätte für Reisende neben der Autobahn konzipiert. Sein Äußeres übersetzt das bekannte Piktogramm einer Kirche in eine dreidimensionale architektonische Form, mit zwei spitzen Türmen, die sich über einem gefalteten weißen Volumen erheben. Altrath fotografiert diese Silhouette aus Nah- und Fernperspektiven und isoliert ihre scharfen Kanten, schrägen Flächen und Öffnungen gegen die Umgebung

items.title: The DFB-Pokal Reimagined
items.summary_original: The DFB-Pokal thrives on contrast: professional clubs facing semi-professional sides, favourites meeting underdogs, and decades of tradition colliding with stories that can unfold in a single night. Its new visual identity seeks to make that tension visible. Introduced for the 2026/27 season, the rebrand brings the men’s, women’s and junior competitions into a shared design system while giving each its own character and expression. At the heart of the new approach is a fundamental question: how can a brand built on consistency capture a competition defined by unpredictability? In this interview, Holger Merk, Head of Brand Department, discusses the thinking behind the new identity, the role of contrast, the balance between tradition and digital culture, and how design can create a framework

items.summary_original: Panter&Tourron’s studio in Lausanne In Switzerland, Panter&Tourron are designing subtle, quiet objects that people can’t help but take notice of. items.title: masks, spirits, and mythical figures carry peruvian heritage into WESR’s murals across europe
items.summary_original: WESR brings together Peruvian heritage and urban culture At the center of WESR’s practice is a continuous movement between places, cultures, and identities. Born in Chiclayo, Peru , in 1980, Danny Figueroa, known as WESR, began painting graffiti in Lima in 1996 before moving to Berlin , where he lives and works today. His practice spans murals, studio painting, illustration , and ceramics . Drawing on the visual traditions of the Peruvian Andes and contemporary urban culture, WESR creates figures that exist between human, animal, and spirit. This relationship between traditional imagery and contemporary graphic language is particularly visible in his murals. items.summary_de: WESR vereint peruanisches Erbe und urbane Kultur. Im Zentrum der WESR-Praxis steht eine kontinuierliche Bewegung zwischen Orten, Kulturen und Identitäten. Seine Praxis umfasst Wandmalerei, Studiomalerei, Illustration und Keramik. Basierend auf den visuellen Traditionen der peruanischen Anden und der zeitgenössischen Stadtkultur schafft WESR Figuren, die zwischen Mensch, Tier und Geist existieren. Diese Beziehung zwischen traditioneller Bildsprache und zeitgenössischer grafischer Sprache wird besonders in seinen Wandgemälden deutlich. Seine Arbeit, die sich durch Graffiti und Malerei im öffentlichen Raum entwickelt hat, trägt Elemente des peruanischen Kulturerbes in neue urbane Räume

The classroom blocks, envelope, and greenery are arranged around this shared outdoor space, making it the core of the school . items.title: Lingo
items.summary_original: Imagine a library. Sealed-in quiet, walls thick as dictionaries. But that's not why you're here — you're at the computer, navigating to your personal linguistic authority: Urban Dictionary. Feverishly typing in the word on your mind since it left your crush's lips in math class: turnt. A thrill washes over you. Not just the definition, but the sight of it: turnt, turned from spoken to serif. Dignified. Elevated. To see slang suited up feels almost subversive. And just right. That's where Softdrive's new typeface, Lingo, comes from. Timeless elegance meets current trend, intellectual authority meets the people's slang. Lingo is both a workhorse, trotting along in body copy, and a show pony, shining in display. This serif respects classical typographic tradition... until it doesn't. Lingo ha

items.title: Celebrating 20 Years of Open Movies
items.summary_original: This year we are celebrating 20 years of making Open Movies. 17 titles, all different and beautiful in their own way. We want to thank you for being a part of this journey – without the community support, all of these projects would not be possible! To celebrate the 20 years of Open Movies in a special way during the Blender Conference 2026, we have created an installation that represents the projects frame by frame. And in the spirit of sharing and being open, visitors of the exhibition can take a frame with them. 20 years of Open Movies exhibition at Blender Conference 2026 Thank you for doing your part. Let’s see what the next decade of open filmmaking will bring!

items.summary_original: the path of the runway rewritten Fashion shows typically begin with a straightforward diagram. Models move along a prescribed path, its edges lined with spectators, and everyone knows where to look. In general this basic layout has remained consistent across time. Yet some of the strongest runway sets begin by disturbing that diagram. Across four decades, designers and scenographers have buried the catwalk beneath the floor, broken it into a grid, or removed the act of walking all together. In these shows, set design shapes much more than just a decorative backdrop. It determines when a model appears and how long they stay visible. It can even determine whether two viewers sitting a few feet apart experience the same sequence. During this season of fashion weeks, we return to ten examples

items.title: Building A UX ROI Case That Survives The Boardroom
items.summary_original: Sooner or later, a CFO looks at your wireframes and asks what any of it actually does for the bottom line. Storyboards don’t answer that question, and the era when a 5-minute pitch could answer it ended, unfortunately, a while ago. These days, if you want to win budget, buy-in, and backing for UX , the design has to be provably good for the business, not only for the people using it. And proving that takes more than taping a dollar sign to a redesign. items.summary_original: ETH ZURICH TRAINS ROBOTIC HAND TO WALK ON ITS FINGERS A robotic hand has apparently decided it no longer needs the rest of the robot . Researchers at ETH Zurich’s Soft Robotics Lab have developed an autonomous five-fingered hand that can walk across different surfaces, steer itself, recover after falling over and interact with objects — all using the same fingers normally reserved for grasping. Rather than adding wheels or legs to the system, the team turns the hand itself into a mobile robot, allowing its fingers to alternate between supporting, moving and manipulating its body. The prototype is based on a commercially available anthropomorphic hand equipped with five fingers and 20 actuated joints, four for each finger. items.summary_de: ETH ZÜRICH TRAINIERT ROBOTERHAND, AUF DEN FINGER ZU GEHEN Eine Roboterhand hat offenbar entschieden, dass sie den Rest des Roboters nicht mehr braucht. Forscher am Soft Robotics Lab der ETH Zürich haben eine autonome fünffingrige Hand entwickelt, die über verschiedene Oberflächen laufen, sich selbst steuern, sich nach einem Sturz erholen und mit Objekten interagieren kann – und das alles mit denselben Fingern, die normalerweise zum Greifen reserviert sind. Anstatt dem System Räder oder Beine hinzuzufügen, verwandelt das Team die Hand selbst in einen mobilen Roboter, der seinen Fingern ermöglicht, seinen Körper abwechselnd zu stützen, zu bewegen und zu manipulieren. Der Prototyp basiert auf einer kommerziell erhältlichen anthropomorphen Hand, die mit fünf Fingern und 20 betätigten Gelenken ausgestattet ist, vier für jeden Finger. Forscher Amirhossein Kazemipour, Hehui Zheng und Robert K. Katzsc
